author: Elizabeth Elkin
description: US lawmakers are preparing to advance a plan that promises to expand the market for corn-based ethanol while scaling back exemptions for oil refineries that don’t use enough of it.
title: Lawmakers Draft Fuel Rules in Possible Hit to Some Refiners

description: Representative Mike Flood (R-NE) states their should be a partnership between government and tech companies when discussing if these large companies should pay for surging power costs. He also shares his reaction to President Trump's hesitation to nominate Kevin Hassett for the Federal Reserve and if he will negotiate with Democrats to provide training & body cameras for ICE agents. Rep. Mike Flood speaks with Joe Mathieu and Julie Fine on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Need a Partnership: Rep. Flood on Big Tech, Energy Costs

description: On today’s Big Take podcast, David Gura and former US Ambassador to China Nicholas Burns talk through China’s role in a changing Western Hemisphere, Trump’s ‘problematic’ focus on Greenland and the pros and perils of the “Donroe Doctrine.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: How The US Changed China’s Calculus in Latin America

description: Rep. Katherine Clark (D-MA) states ICE is a reign of terror and needs accountability when discussing her hearing in Minnesota about people impacted by ICE raids. She also voices her frustration with her Republican colleagues over continued health care issues. Representative Clark speaks with Joe Mathieu and Julie Fine on Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power: Late Edition.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: ICE is a Reign of Terror, Need Accountability: Rep. Clark

author: Iain Marlow
description: The White House has named the members of an executive panel as part of a so-called Board of Peace that’s intended implement President Donald Trump’s peace plan for the Gaza Strip.
title: White House Unveils Gaza Board of Peace Executive Board

description: Daron Acemoglu, Institute Professor in the Department of Economics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss his 'Theory of Trump' as the second year of President Trump's second term begins. Acemoglu argues that most of the administration’s actions — including crypto dealings, the appointment of unqualified allies to high-level positions, unconstitutional deportations and National Guard deployments, and the ouster of a Latin American head of state — all follow a certain logic, as President Trump looks to expand executive power. Acemoglu speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Nobel Prize-Winning Economist Offers a Unified Theory of Trump

author: David Gura, Rachael Lewis-Krisky
description: Former Ambassador Nicholas Burns on China’s plans in Venezuela, Greenland’s future and the pros and perils of Trump’s ‘Donroe Doctrine.’
title: How the US Changed China’s Calculus in Latin America

description: On today's episode, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Michael Shepard, Bloomberg News Senior Editor for Technology & Strategic Industries, about Trump's move to have tech giants pay for surging power costs. They also speak with Leslie Marks Chief Investment Officer for Equities at Mackenzie Investments about the biggest risks to investments in 2026. Finally, they speak with Daron Acemoglu, Institute Professor in the Department of Economics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, about his Bloomberg Businessweek article detailing his “Unified Theory of Trump," and Maja Vujinovic, CEO of Digital Assets at FG Nexus, on recent volatility in the cryptocurrency sector. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He’ll Make Tech Firms Pay for Power  | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 1/16/2026

description: Mackenzie Investments Equities CIO Lesley Marks joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss her 2026 market outlook, including her call for a global broadening of positive market sentiment and trade in 2026, including emerging markets. She also weighs in on the lack of market worry as several major geopolitical events kick off the year. Marks speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Market Rally Will Broaden Globally in 2026: Mackenzie's Marks

description: Bloomberg News US Semiconductor Reporter Ian King discusses the latest TSMC earnings report and what lies ahead for the chip maker with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: TSMC Eyes Smaller Gap Between US, Taiwan Chipmaking

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: The president plans to outline more of his plans to address affordability.
title: Trump Bringing His Populist Pitch to the Davos Elite

author: Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump offered to resume US mediation of a long-running water dispute between Egypt and Ethiopia as he seeks to avert conflict over a dam that could significantly alter the Nile River.
title: Trump Offers to Mediate Egypt-Ethiopia Nile Dam Dispute

author: Andreina Itriago, Patricia Laya
description: In Venezuela, much of the choreography of power looks just as it did before Nicolás Maduro’s capture by US Special Forces.
title: Venezuela’s Rodríguez Consolidates Power After Maduro Ouster

description: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright talks about efforts that are underway to have technology companies build new power plants without raising electric prices for Americans. He speaks to Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall at the White House.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Shovels in Ground for New Power Plants, Wright Says

author: Liam Knox, Josyana Joshua
description: The Trump administration has paused its efforts to seize student debt from borrowers’ paychecks, the Education Department said Friday, as the White House makes a concerted push around an affordability agenda ahead of this year’s midterm elections.
title: Trump Delays Seizing Wages of Student Borrowers as Affordability Push Ramps Up

description: Dana Stroul, The Washington Institute for Near East Policy Research Director, states she hasn't seen or heard any proof that killings and executions in Iran have stopped. She also talks about expecting to hear more devastating news from Iran in the coming days and shares her thoughts on President Trump holding off attacking the country. Dana speaks with Joe Mathieu and Julie Fine on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power: Late Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: No Proof Killings in Iran Have Stopped: Dana Stroul

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discuss the latest geopolitical news. On today's show, Council on Foreign Relations President Emeritus Richard Haass, Harvard Kennedy School’s Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Republican Main Street Partnership President and CEO Sarah Chamberlain and Groundwork Collaborative Senior Strategic Advisor Kitty Richards. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Decisions Loom On Iran, Greenland | Balance of Power: Early Edition 1/16/2026

description: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro comments on how the electricity grid should handle all of this new power from data centers. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Pennsylvania Governor Shapiro on Extending PJM Price Cap

description: Richard Haass, president emeritus of Council on Foreign Relations, said the US can get whatever economic or military arrangements it wants with Greenland so pressuring or bullying another NATO member is unnecessary. Haass also weighed in on President Trump's meeting with Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, saying that while Machado tried to play Trump by giving him her Nobel Peace Prize, she got played in the end.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Greenland Policy 'Unnecessary' and 'Misguided,' Says Richard Haass

author: Michelle Ma, Alicia Tang
description: US President Donald Trump is calling for an emergency wholesale electricity auction that, his administration says, will force technology companies to pay for the new power they need to run massive AI data centers under construction across the country.
title: Trump Says He’ll Make Tech Firms Pay for Power. They’d Love To

description: Peter Atwater, president of Financial Insyghts, said that President Trump's recent turn toward affordability policies that are in line with left-leaning politicians like Elizabeth Warren and Zohran Mamdani says more about his desire to survive politically rather than his true ideology. Atwater described the current moment as an 'arms race' on affordability ahead of the midterms as both Democrats and Republicans try to connect with voters.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Affordability 'Arms Race' Taking Place Before Midterms, Says Atwater

author: Eliyahu Kamisher, Biz Carson
description: A proposed tax on California’s wealthiest residents is drawing opposition from a growing group of top state Democrats, including a US representative for Silicon Valley and Katie Porter, the former congresswoman now running for governor.
title: Billionaire Tax Plan Draws Fire From California Top Democrats

author: Jef Feeley
description: The US Supreme Court agreed to hear Bayer AG’s appeal taking aim at thousands of lawsuits targeting its top-selling Roundup weedkiller for causing cancer.
title: Bayer Gets Supreme Court Hearing in Challenge to Roundup Suits

description:
President Donald Trump said he would hold off on invoking the Insurrection Act after previously threatening to use the law to deploy US military troops in Minnesota.
“I don’t think there’s any reason right now to use it,” Trump told reporters on Friday as he departed the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He’ll Forgo Sending US Troops to Minnesota For Now: Q&A

author: Courtney Subramanian
description: President Donald Trump said he would hold off on invoking the Insurrection Act after previously threatening to use the law to deploy US military troops in Minnesota.
title: Trump Says He’ll Forgo Sending Troops to Minnesota for Now

description: María Corina Machado's decision to gift her Nobel Peace Prize medal to Donald Trump left some in Norway stunned. Heidi Taksdal Skjeseth explains.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Shock in Norway as Machado Gifts Trump Nobel Peace Medal

description:
Could Donald Trump order a fresh strike on Iran?

New Hampshire Democrat Senator Jeanne Shaheen warns that US military action may have unintended consequences. Subscribe to The Mishal Husain Show wherever you get your podcasts. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Military Action in Iran Risks Backlash: Shaheen

author: David Voreacos, Zachary R Mider, Hadriana Lowenkron
description: A San Diego businesswoman who was granted clemency by Donald Trump in 2021 and later convicted on new fraud charges received a pardon from the president on Thursday, according to a White House official who spoke on the condition of anonymity.
title: Trump Pardons Convicted Fraudster After Earlier Clemency Grant

description: President Donald Trump expressed reluctance toward nominating Kevin Hassett as Federal Reserve chair, casting further doubt over his search for the next head of the central bank.  Bloomberg's Stuart Paul joins to discuss on Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Voices Reluctance at Nominating Hassett as Fed Chair

author: Jonathan Browning
description: The populist Reform party is suing the UK government, challenging proposals that may delay local elections, according to a court order.
title: Reform Sues UK Government Over Possible Local Election Delay

description: "It seems like a miracle to be sitting here in a free country," said María Corina Machado, a Venezuelan opposition leader, while speaking at the Heritage Foundation in Washington. Machado says Venezuela is undergoing a true transition to democracy. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Machado Says Venezuela Is Undergoing a True Transition to Democracy

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Naureen S Malik
description: The Trump administration laid out a plan intended to compel technology companies to effectively fund the construction of new power plants as a way to tame surging consumer utility bills while aiding the development of data centers.
title: Trump Pushes for Emergency Power Auction to Fuel AI Boom

description: Republicans likely only have a year left to accomplish their agenda – and they don't know what they want, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Abby McCloskey says. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The GOP Is Running Out of Time

author: Skylar Woodhouse, Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump urged Republican lawmakers to quickly move on a White House healthcare plan, seeking to shift the narrative on an issue that threatens his party’s hold on Congress with millions of Americans facing premium hikes or the risk of lost coverage.
title: Trump Presses GOP to Move Health Plan as Premium Hikes Loom

author: Greg Stohr
description: The US Supreme Court scheduled Tuesday as its next opinion day amid a worldwide wait for a ruling on President Donald Trump’s signature tariffs.
title: Supreme Court Sets Tuesday for Next Opinions With Tariff Ruling Pending

author: Ben Bartenstein, Eric Martin, Natalia Drozdiak
description: A senior envoy for Venezuela’s new government is set to meet with US officials in Washington on Friday, according to people familiar with the matter, as the White House firms up its relationship with acting President Delcy Rodriguez’s administration in Caracas.
title: Venezuela Envoy in Washington After CIA Chief Visits Caracas

author: Golnar Motevalli
description: A man who’s been a polarizing figure for Iranians for years has become a focal point for the biggest ever popular rebuke of the Islamic Republic. That underscores just how exasperated Iranians have become.
title: Iran's Exiled Prince Is Buoyed by Nation Desperate for Change

author: Lucy White
description: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage will attend the World Economic Forum summit in Davos next week for the first time, as he attempts to cement his position as one of Britain’s most influential politicians on the world stage as well as at home.
title: Reform UK’s Farage to Attend Davos Despite Criticizing WEF

author: Melissa Shin
description: The leader of Canada’s main automaking province swiftly criticized a new trade deal with China that lowers Beijing’s tariffs on Canadian canola in exchange for eased import rules on Chinese electric vehicles.
title: Ontario’s Doug Ford Slams Canada-China Trade Deal as Threat to Auto Jobs

author: Jorge Valero
description: The European Parliament is considering linking approval of a massive US trade deal to Donald Trump backing down from his threats to take over Greenland, putting further strain on an agreement already facing opposition.
title: EU Parliament Eyes Tying US Trade Deal Approval to Greenland

author: Donato Paolo Mancini
description: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government aims to intensify its approach to the Arctic as Western allies grapple with how to contain China and Russia’s presence in the region and as President Donald Trump threatens to take control of Greenland.
title: Meloni Seeks to Boost Italy’s Foreign Policy Clout in the Arctic

author: Daniel Basteiro
description: The US is blocking Spain from preparations for its G-20 summit as relations sour between the countries, the latest sign of the Trump administration’s willingness to sideline allies in its push to reshape the global order.
title: Spain Shut Out as US Embraces Trump’s Allies for G-20 Planning

author: Santosh Kumar
description: India’s trade deal with the European Union will include some agricultural products while excluding items that could harm domestic farmers, a senior official in New Delhi said, as the two sides inch closer to signing an agreement that has been under negotiation for years.
title: India and EU Trade Deal to Include Some Farm Goods, Official Says

description: The dramatic sacking of a senior Conservative and his defection hours later to Nigel Farage's Reform UK all-but ended the chances of any deal to unite the British right, confirming the next general election as the most widely contested in decades. Some Tories had held out hopes they could forge a pact with the insurgent Reform party that has rapidly eclipsed them in voter affections. The fallout from leader Kemi Badenoch's shock decision to fire her rival Robert Jenrick on Thursday put that further from reach. Our UK Politics Reporter James Woolcock joined Caroline Hepker and Lizzy Burden on Bloomberg Radio to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Why Jenrick’s Reform Defection Fractures UK Political Right

author: Weilun Soon
description: An oil tanker that shows up on maritime databases as having never existed U-turned as it headed toward German waters and is now sailing in the direction of Russia’s Arctic coast.
title: Russia-Bound Phantom Oil Tanker U-Turns Away From Baltic Sea

author: Sakura Murakami
description: The conservative leader’s gamble could consolidate her power or trigger a period of prolonged political uncertainty.
title: Japanese Premier Takaichi Stakes All on Unpredictable Election

author: Erik Wasson, Ken Tran
description: The US Congress is set to avoid another government shutdown later this month by passing compromise bills that would soften spending cuts sought by the Trump administration, according to Republicans and Democrats involved in the process.
title: Congress on Track to Avoid Shutdown and Soften Trump Spending Cuts

author: Georgie McKay
description: President Donald Trump’s unexpected demand for a cap on credit card interest rates sent financial shares tumbling this week, while leaving the heads of Wall Street’s biggest lenders fielding a swarm of questions on their quarterly earnings calls.
title: Trump’s Credit Card Threats Rain on Big Banks’ Earnings Parade

author: Arsalan Shahla
description: Iran is enduring its most extensive internet blackout on record, activists say, raising fears that Tehran’s crackdown on protesters may persist despite assurances it would ease punishments.
title: Iran’s Record Internet Block Stokes Fears Crackdown May Continue

author: Enda Curran, Jonnelle Marte, Saleha Mohsin
description: The Trump administration’s latest attack on the Federal Reserve has stoked expectations that Jerome Powell will stay on the Board of Governors after his term as chair ends in May — setting up the optics of a rival center of influence inside the world’s most powerful central bank, even if Powell doesn’t want it.
title: Trump’s Pursuit of Powell Threatens to Muddle Fed Tea Leaves

description: A group of US senators is set to meet members of the Danish parliament in Copenhagen on Friday. Nuuk and Copenhagen are seeking to achieve support from Capitol Hill that could help constrain any future moves by the White House to threaten Greenland. Bloomberg’s Sara Sjolin reports.
title: Denmark, Greenland Step Up Lobbying of US Lawmakers

author: Ott Ummelas, Heidi Taksdal Skjeseth
description: Norway reacted with disbelief to the news that Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado gave her medal to US President Donald Trump, who has long coveted the award.
title: Norway Stunned After Machado Gifts Nobel Peace Prize Medal to Trump

author: Claudia Cohen
description: A senior Natixis banker said many European arms companies have seen few orders so far despite vows from the region’s governments to dramatically step up military spending.
title: EU Defense Firms Still Waiting for Government Boom, Natixis Says

author: Daniel Hornak
description: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico will meet US President Donald Trump at his Mar-a-Lago resort on Saturday, his office said, in a bid to strengthen ties between Washington and a European Union member state that’s been sharply critical of the bloc.
title: Slovak Premier Fico to Meet Trump in a Bid to Strengthen US Ties

author: William Horobin
description: France’s government will make fresh proposals on the 2026 budget on Friday after halting a parliamentary debate that was heading for failure.
title: France’s Lecornu to Revise Budget Amid Blocked Parliament

author: Slav Okov
description: The euro area’s latest member Bulgaria will hold a snap election in the coming months, its eighth in five years as the Balkan nation fails to break an extended cycle of political deadlock.
title: Bulgaria to Hold Snap Vote as Crisis Grows After Euro Entry

author: Simon Marks, Sam Dagher
description: Saudi Arabia is finalizing an agreement on a new military coalition with Somalia and Egypt, part of its bid to curtail the United Arab Emirates’ regional influence.
title: Saudi Arabia in Talks With Egypt, Somalia on Military Coalition

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, US President Donald Trump has accepted Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado's Nobel Peace Prize medal, calling it a great honor.

The US and Taiwan struck a trade deal that will cut tariffs on goods from the island to 15% and see Taiwanese chip companies increase financing for American operations by $500 billion.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney hailed his strategic partnership with China’s Xi Jinping, hours after touting the importance of their ties in the face of the “new world order”.

Today's guests: Sunaina Haldea, Global head of private capital advisory at Raymond James. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Machado Presents Peace Prize to Trump & US-Taiwan Tariff Deal | Daybreak Europe 1/16/2026

author: Hallie Gu, Brian Platt
description: Canada expects China to cut tariffs on its rapeseed by March 1, which would be a significant thaw in a trade rift that has disrupted crop flows and tested bilateral relations.
title: Canada Says China to Ease Canola Tariffs by March in Trade Thaw

author: Fred Ojambo
description: Ugandan leader Yoweri Museveni held a commanding lead in the East African nation’s presidential elections, partial vote tallies showed, placing him on course to win a seventh term.
title: Partial Uganda Vote Tally Points to Landslide Win for Museveni

author: Rene Vollgraaff
description: The US criticized South Africa for allowing Iran to participate in naval drills off the coast of Cape Town, after conflicting reports about the Islamic Republic’s involvement in the exercises.
title: US Says South Africa Is Cozying Up to Iran With Naval Drills

description: Decades of Western sanctions have supercharged the rise of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps from a branch of the military established to protect the 1979 Islamic revolution to a gargantuan economic and political force. The IRGC’s influence will not end even if it puts down the protests and it will play a pivotal role in what happens next. Bloomberg’s Patrick Sykes reports.
title: Why Iran’s Fate Lies in the Revolutionary Guards’ Hands

author: Sanne Wass, Sara Sjolin
description: President Donald Trump threatened fresh tariffs on goods from nations that oppose his push to take control of Greenland, stepping up his rhetoric while Denmark hosted US lawmakers on its home turf following meetings in Washington this week.
title: Trump Floats Levies Over Greenland as Denmark Lobbies Congress

author: Marilen Martin
description: Germany is set to start a major subsidy program for electric vehicles worth €3 billion ($3.5 billion), renewing efforts to push sales and support one of its key industries.
title: Germany to Hand EV Buyers Up to €6,000 a Car to Boost Demand

author: Olesia Safronova, Volodymyr Verbianyi
description: As President Zelenskiy declares an energy emergency, citizens seek out heat where they can.
title: With the Power Out, Kyiv’s Residents Confront Cold as a Weapon of War

author: Brian Platt, Lucille Liu, Colum Murphy
description: China and Canada reached a wide-ranging agreement to lower trade barriers and rebuild ties, signaling a pivot in Canadian foreign policy and a break from alignment with Donald Trump’s trade agenda.
title: Canada Inks Trade Truce With China in Break From Trump’s Agenda
